tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_ae.classification_evidence: Interval crosses zero; not a resolved sign and no positive-control bound was run for this specific arm.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_ae.description: Shade the tiebreaker last-game total guess 1 point below the market total (predeclared LEAD-54 direction). Metric: mean absolute error improvement (candidate minus served, positive favours the shade) against the raw served market-total guess, closest-total tiebreak reading, all REG last-games-of-week 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_ae.notes: Season-blocked bootstrap, 4000 draws, seed 20260910. Served baseline = raw schedules total_line (offset 0), common random numbers used against the simulated public field for every offset.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_ae.plain_summary: Guessing 1 point lower than the betting market's total for the week's last game came a hair closer to the real final score than guessing the market number exactly, on 17 seasons of games.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_exact.classification_evidence: Interval crosses zero; this is a secondary metric because POL-12 never recorded which rule the pool actually uses.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_exact.description: Alternative reading of the pool's undocumented tiebreak rule: closest EXACT SCORE (Manhattan distance on home/away points) instead of closest total. -1 point shade vs the served guess, both scores built from the market margin plus the (shaded) total, rounded; mean distance improvement, 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_exact.plain_summary: If the pool actually judges the tiebreaker by the exact final score rather than just the combined total, shading the total down by 1 point did not clearly help and leaned slightly the other way.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_exact.description: Exact-score tiebreak reading, -1 point shade, win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6), 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_exact.plain_summary: Under the exact-score reading of the pool's rule, shading the total down by 1 point did not win more tiebreakers than the plain market-based guess.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_oos_a.description: Chronological out-of-sample check: the -1 point shade (LEAD-54's predeclared direction, and the shade the AE metric alone would have chosen from 2009-2017) scored on the held-out 2018-2025 seasons only. Mean absolute error improvement vs the served market-total guess, closest-total reading.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_oos_a.notes: Trained (shade choice only, by AE improvement) on 2009-2017; scored here strictly on 2018-2025, no re-selection.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_oos_a.plain_summary: Picking the 1-point-under shade using only the older seasons, then testing it on the newer seasons, still showed the same small edge -- it did not fall apart out of sample.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_oos_w.description: Same chronological out-of-sample check as the AE version, scored instead as tie-break win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6), 2018-2025 held-out seasons.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_oos_w.plain_summary: On the newer seasons held back for testing, the 1-point shade still did not clearly win more tiebreakers against a crowd that leans toward overs.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_winra.description: Same -1 point shade, scored instead as tie-break WIN RATE against a simulated public field (public guess ~ market total + Normal(mean=+1.5, sd=6), declared before scoring): win-rate improvement in percentage points vs the served (unshaded) guess.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_winra.notes: Public field: mean offset +1.5, sd 6.0, 20000 Monte Carlo draws per game, common random numbers vs the served arm.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus1_winra.plain_summary: Against a crowd of guessers who tend to pick a slightly-too-high final score, shading our own guess down by 1 point did not clearly win more tiebreakers than just using the market number.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus2_ae.description: Shade the tiebreaker last-game total guess 2 points below the market total. Mean absolute error improvement vs the served market-total guess, closest-total reading, 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus2_ae.plain_summary: Guessing 2 points lower than the market total also landed a bit closer to the real score on average, though less clearly than the 1-point shade.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus2_winra.description: -2 point shade, tie-break win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6).
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus2_winra.plain_summary: Shading 2 points low did not win more tiebreakers than the plain market guess against a crowd that leans toward overs.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_ae.classification_evidence: Interval crosses zero (upper bound +0.277), so wrong_sign_resolved is inadmissible despite the negative point estimate.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_ae.description: -3 point shade, mean absolute error improvement vs the served market-total guess, closest-total reading, 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_ae.plain_summary: Guessing 3 points under the market total started to cost accuracy on average, though the result is still too uncertain to call it worse for sure.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_winra.classification_evidence: Interval crosses zero (upper bound +0.231), so wrong_sign_resolved is inadmissible even though probability_positive is only 0.037.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_winra.description: -3 point shade, tie-break win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6).
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus3_winra.plain_summary: Shading 3 points low leaned toward losing more tiebreakers than the plain market guess, but the result is still too uncertain to call it settled.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus4_ae.description: -4 point shade, mean absolute error improvement vs the served market-total guess, closest-total reading, 2009-2025.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus4_ae.plain_summary: Guessing 4 points under the market total was worse on average than just using the market number, though this particular read of the result is still uncertain.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus4_winra.classification_evidence: Whole 95% interval [-6.782, -0.813] sits below zero: a 4-point low shade is resolvably worse than the served guess on tie-break win rate against the declared public field. This closes the -4 arm on this metric only; it does not close the -1/-2 arms, which are separate cells.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus4_winra.description: -4 point shade, tie-break win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6). Whole interval sits below zero.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_minus4_winra.plain_summary: Shading the guess a full 4 points under the market total clearly won FEWER tiebreakers than just using the market number, against a crowd that leans toward overs -- shading that far is a mistake.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_model_lean_a.description: Shade the total by the already-served 0.1 x model-predicted-residual blend (nfl_ats.tiebreaker.TOTALS_RESIDUAL_WEIGHT, reused not re-derived) instead of a fixed offset, i.e. a shade proportional to the model's own under/over lean. Mean absolute error improvement vs the raw market-total guess, restricted to last-games-of-week with a walk-forward model prediction (2010-2025).
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_model_lean_a.plain_summary: Letting the computer model's own guess about whether a game will go over or under nudge the tiebreaker number did not clearly beat just using the market's own number.

tiebreaker_low_side_shading_model_lean_w.description: Model-lean-proportional shade (0.1 x predicted_residual), tie-break win rate vs the served guess against the declared simulated public field (mean +1.5, sd 6), 2010-2025 model-covered games.
tiebreaker_low_side_shading_model_lean_w.plain_summary: Using the model's own lean to nudge the tiebreaker guess did not clearly win more tiebreakers than the plain market guess.
